info.name: ft_transcendence | Authentication + Standard User Management (Demo v1.2)
info.description: v1-style ordered demo: Authentication and Standard User Management with 104 HTTP requests. Each run generates 3 fresh development-only test users; explicit per-user sid headers and disabled cookie jar keep sessions isolated. Upload fixture file paths use the single collection variable fixtures_dir, default tests/postman/fixtures relative to the Postman working directory. Run all folders in order; the suite writes to the dev DB and does not delete user accounts. The Socket.IO event lifecycle is out of scope for HTTP-only requests. See README-user-management.md.

item.name: 00 — Setup and baseline
item.description: Run this folder first. Each run generates unique demo accounts; they are not deleted by the API.

item.name: 00.1 — Initialize a fresh run and confirm backend health

request.description: Regenerates test identifiers and empties old temporary SID variables. No cleanup or destructive database operation.

exec: pm.test("Application and PostgreSQL healthy", () => { const h = pm.response.json().data; pm.expect(h.status).to.eql("ok"); pm.expect(h.database).to.eql("ok"); });
run_id: id, run_marker: marker, demo_password: 'Demo!' + id + '-42a',
ada_name: marker + '-Ada', bob_name: marker + '-Bob', carol_name: marker + '-Carol_100%'
console.log('New user-management run marker:', marker, '(three new accounts will be created)');

item.name: 01 — Registration
item.description: Fresh accounts Ada, Bob, Carol; field validation and email uniqueness. Requires setup.

request.description: POST /auth/register creates a user but does not log in / establish a session.

exec: pm.test("Ada email normalized and name saved", () => {pm.expect(data.email).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get("ada_email"));pm.expect(data.displayName).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get("ada_name"));});

request.description: POST /auth/register creates a user but does not log in / establish a session.

exec: pm.test("Bob email normalized and name saved", () => {pm.expect(data.email).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get("bob_email"));pm.expect(data.displayName).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get("bob_name"));});

request.description: POST /auth/register creates a user but does not log in / establish a session.

exec: pm.test("Carol email normalized and name saved", () => {pm.expect(data.email).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get("carol_email"));pm.expect(data.displayName).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get("carol_name"));});

item.name: 02 — Authentication and sessions
item.description: Wrong credentials, login DTO validation, distinct session cookies for three accounts, /auth/me and invalid session. Avoid login brute-force/rate-limit experiments during this run.

request.description: The response cookie is stored in a Postman collection variable for distinct user sessions. Never export or commit live SID values.

exec: pm.test("SID cookie set, HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax", () => {pm.expect(sidMatch).to.not.eql(null); pm.expect(cookieHeader).to.include("HttpOnly"); pm.expect(cookieHeader).to.include("Secure"); pm.expect(cookieHeader).to.include("SameSite=Lax");});

request.description: The response cookie is stored in a Postman collection variable for distinct user sessions. Never export or commit live SID values.

exec: pm.test("SID cookie set, HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax", () => {pm.expect(sidMatch).to.not.eql(null); pm.expect(cookieHeader).to.include("HttpOnly"); pm.expect(cookieHeader).to.include("Secure"); pm.expect(cookieHeader).to.include("SameSite=Lax");});

request.description: The response cookie is stored in a Postman collection variable for distinct user sessions. Never export or commit live SID values.

exec: pm.test("SID cookie set, HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax", () => {pm.expect(sidMatch).to.not.eql(null); pm.expect(cookieHeader).to.include("HttpOnly"); pm.expect(cookieHeader).to.include("Secure"); pm.expect(cookieHeader).to.include("SameSite=Lax");});

item.name: 03 — Profiles and authorization
item.description: Public profile contains only id/displayName/avatarUrl; PATCH /users/me updates only the authenticated user.

item.name: 03.1 — Bob public profile read as Ada (200)

exec: pm.test("Name is trimmed and only Ada changed", () => {pm.expect(data.id).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get("ada_id")); pm.expect(data.displayName).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get("run_marker") + "-AdaUpdated");});

item.name: 04 — Public User Search
item.description: Tests case-insensitivity, privacy, caller exclusion, limits, LIKE literal underscore, and validation. Search is not an email lookup.

exec: pm.test("Search finds Bob and Carol, excludes Ada", () => {pm.expect(data).to.be.an("array"); const ids=data.map(u=>u.id);pm.expect(ids).to.include(pm.collectionVariables.get("bob_id"));pm.expect(ids).to.include(pm.collectionVariables.get("carol_id"));pm.expect(ids).to.not.include(pm.collectionVariables.get("ada_id"));});
pm.test("Only public fields in every result", () => data.forEach(u=>pm.expect(Object.keys(u).sort()).to.eql(["avatarUrl","displayName","id"])));
pm.test("Carol with literal underscore found", () => pm.expect(data.some(u => u.id === pm.collectionVariables.get("carol_id"))).to.eql(true));

item.name: 05 — Friends: complete lifecycle
item.description: Order-sensitive workflow: send -> duplicate/reverse prevention -> incoming/outgoing -> unauthorized accept -> accept -> presence snapshot -> unfriend -> decline/cancel. Re-running a single step out of order may cause conflicts.

exec: pm.test("Outgoing includes Bob", () => {pm.expect(data.incoming).to.eql([]);pm.expect(data.outgoing.some(r => r.id === pm.collectionVariables.get("request_id") && r.user.id === pm.collectionVariables.get("bob_id"))).to.eql(true);});
pm.test("Incoming from Ada", () => pm.expect(data.incoming.some(r => r.id === pm.collectionVariables.get("request_id") && r.user.id === pm.collectionVariables.get("ada_id"))).to.eql(true));

item.name: 05.13a — Outsider cannot decline an unrelated pending request (404)
05.13b — Pending request is not yet an accepted friend (404)
05.16 — Ada friends include Bob + isOnline boolean (200)
05.26 — Declined request cannot be deleted twice (404)
06 — Avatar uploads (local files required)
item.description: Optional file-backed folder: first attach three fixtures in Postman (or run with Newman using correct working directory). Do not claim fully automated portable uploads without their fixtures. No user cleanup on completion.

request.description: Explicit empty multipart body: backend requires a single image file.
Requires valid PNG fixture even though global session guard should block first.
Requires tests/postman/fixtures/um-avatar.png. In Postman desktop, select the bundled PNG in the file picker. Browser Origin may be omitted by Postman.

exec: pm.test("Avatar URL generated for own ID", () => pm.expect(data.avatarUrl).to.eql("/api/v1/users/"+pm.collectionVariables.get("ada_id")+"/avatar"));

item.name: 06.3 — Bob can view Ada image: WebP binary (200)
06.4 — Public profile exposes generated avatar URL (200)

exec: pm.test("Avatar URL stays stable on replacement", () => pm.expect(data.avatarUrl).to.eql("/api/v1/users/"+pm.collectionVariables.get("ada_id")+"/avatar"));

request.description: Requires tests/postman/fixtures/um-invalid.txt (not a real image). Existing valid avatar should remain.

exec: pm.test("Uploaded malformed bytes (not a missing file)", () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().error.details.file).to.include("Invalid or unsupported image"));

request.description: Extra form field is rejected (files=1 fields=0 parts=1).
An untrusted Origin is forbidden. Depending on gateway rules the 403 may come from WAF or backend; this request does not attribute it.

exec: pm.test("Forbidden upload does not return success", () => pm.expect(pm.response.code).to.eql(403));
pm.test("Backend origin guard rejected the request", () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().error.code).to.eql("INVALID_ORIGIN"));

item.name: 06.9 — Avatar remains available after rejected replacements (200)
07 — Presence (HTTP prerequisites, not live realtime)
item.description: The full online/offline and friend-only events require socket.io-client. This folder intentionally avoids claiming those results based on an HTTP 200 handshake.

request.description: HTTP alone cannot mark users online. After section 05 unfriend, the list is expected to be empty. To test actual presence transitions, use an authenticated Socket.IO client and an accepted friendship.

exec: pm.test("Presence snapshot is an array", () => pm.expect(data).to.be.an("array"));

request.description: IMPORTANT: This only validates transport-level opening; it does NOT authenticate the Socket.IO namespace, mark Ada online or verify presence:changed. A real socket.io-client is needed for those.

item.name: 08 — Logout, SID revocation and session isolation
item.description: Logout invalidates only the current session. End here to discard locally captured SID values. Created user accounts intentionally remain in dev database.

item.name: 08.3 — Ada old SID rejected after logout (401)
08.4 — Bob remains authenticated after Ada logs out (200)
